additional_info.subject: Urgent – Critical Support Request | Two Incidents and Station Shutdown at Delek Mitzpe Ramon (Serial No. 170000467)
additional_info.body:
Dear Siemens Support Team,
We are reporting two consecutive technical incidents at the Delek Mitzpe Ramon charging site in Israel, related to chargers with Serial Number 170000467.
Following these events, the station has been shut down and is currently out of service.
This station is one of the most critical DC charging points in our operational network.
We urgently require your technical assessment and immediate recommendations for safe recovery.
---
First Incident – CCS2 Connector Overheating (04/07/2025)
During a charging session at the CCS2 (DC2) outlet, the customer noticed a burning smell near the vehicle's inlet.
The charging cable could not be released, even after attempting manual release from the vehicle.
Eventually, the customer pressed the emergency stop button on the charger.
Key Findings:
Emergency stop was triggered at 14:56:04 Israel time (13:56:04 Germany time)
All connectors switched to FAULTED state with error code SafetyRelay_QA26
Charger logs recorded a fault from the DC2 cable temperature sensor
The customer reported partial melting of the connector inside the vehicle's inlet
---
Second Incident – Vehicle Fault After Connecting to DC1 (Approx. One Hour Later)
Another customer reported that after connecting the DC cable to DC1, the vehicle displayed a fault and is unable to start or drive. The customer attributes the issue to the charger.
Technical Analysis:
Charger logs indicate an insulation fault (IMD_BC1) detected immediately after cable connection
Measured insulation value: 311 kOhm
The system transitioned to FAULTED state, and converters were disconnected
---
Current Status and Urgency:
The charging station has been fully shut down following safety protocols
This is one of our most important DC charging locations, with significant operational impact
Immediate technical support is required to diagnose the root cause, validate system integrity, and return the station to service safely
---
Requested Actions:
Urgent technical review of both incidents and system logs
Recommendations for on-site inspection and safe system recovery
Additional guidance to prevent recurrence of similar issues
We appreciate your prompt feedback and full cooperation to resolve this critical situation. All relevant log files are available upon request.
Thank you in advance,
Ziv Vinitzer
Head of DC Charging

additional_info.subject: Re: Urgent – Critical Support Request | Two Incidents and Station Shutdown at Delek Mitzpe Ramon (Serial No. 170000467) CRM:00921001732
additional_info.body:
Dear Siemens Team,
Following recent events reported with the SICHARGE D system, we encountered an issue during one of the PE-PP-CUT tests performed using a Comemso system.
Summary of Findings:
On a specific output of the dispenser, the test result was FAILED, with a measured PP-Res value that was negative or abnormal (e.g., -138.6Ω), under the DIN70121 protocol.
The main unit (Main Cabinet) successfully passed the same test without any irregularities.
Additionally, DC1 and DC2 outputs of the same dispenser successfully passed the test, with typical PP-Res values around 131Ω, under an ISO15118 test scenario.
We kindly request your review and clarification regarding the following:
1. What could cause a negative or abnormal PP-Res value on the specific dispenser output.
2. Could the difference in test protocols (DIN70121 vs. ISO15118) explain the variance in results.
3. What tests or actions do you recommend to identify or resolve the issue at the dispenser and the specific output.
4. Are there any system parameters or configurations that could affect the PE-PP-CUT test results.
We appreciate your support and recommendations for next steps.
Best regards,
Ziv Vinitzer
Head of DC Charging

additional_info.subject: ID0435701-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P4 170000467] Station out of service CRM:00315002798
additional_info.body:
Hi Ziv, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well.
I checked your photos from the comenso.
1. What could cause a negative or abnormal PP-Res value on the specific dispenser output:
According to physics in general, it should be impossible to have negative resistance in a ordinary system.
Tomorrow I will go to the factory and test the same in our dispenser.
If we find the same value, I would have to understand what is causing this and how we can resolve it.
If we do not find the same value, I would need to have from your side:
Certificate of calibration of Comenso
Logs from the comenso
The logs we can get them via software that you can ask via email to the comenso team. They will ask for the comenso Serial Number and use the cable that comes with the box to transfer the data. All of this should be explained in the manual.
2. Could the difference in test protocols (DIN70121 vs. ISO15118) explain the variance in results.
This is a very deep and detailed answer which could take a long time to formalize. The DIN norm has +300 pages and ISO15118 has at least 4 different norms (ISO15118-2,3,20,etc) which contains +1000 pages.
3. What tests or actions do you recommend to identify or resolve the issue at the dispenser and the specific output.
The best that we can do is measure the PP in the charger at the same time it's plugged when we have the negative resistance.
4. Are there any system parameters or configurations that could affect the PE-PP-CUT test results.
The only use we have for the Comenso is to test charging sessions to make sure the outlets are working. We haven't tried all the tests in detail.
I checked this charger and from the last 7 days, there were 15 sucessfull sessions in DC3 and DC4, together, so in terms of operability there is nothing wrong.
Tomorrow I will provide you feedback from my tests.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0435701-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P4 170000467] Station out of service CRM:00315002798
additional_info.body:
Hi Ziv,
I performed the tests just now in a SiD300 with dispenser dual plug and here are the results, I will send the photo in attachment:
*Photo1 - Comparison between DIN with comenso box*
As you can see, we have a resistance of 1.3kOhm. I made a normal session with ISO and still we have the exact same result.
I believe that there must be either a miss connection or a leakage that makes the resistance drop, or the comenso has some kind of issue.
I would recommend confirming with another charging station if you measure the same value, I tested in the DC2 (main charger) and we still see 1.3kOhm. DC2.jpeg
Since the sessions are all running properly, the only thing we could do is test with a EV that uses DIN and prove that it will fail. If it doesn't then I would recommend checking what's wrong with the comenso box.
Let me know your thought and questions.
Thanks!
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: Re:‏ ID0435701-DC/Si-D/IL-[MP / P4 170000467] Station out of service CRM:00315002798
additional_info.body:
Hello,
Following up on our correspondence regarding the critical incident that occurred at Sicharge D MP / P4 170000467 on 04/07/2025, we would like to know when we can expect to receive your investigation report.
For your convenience, below is the event timeline as documented on our side:
Event Timeline:
First Incident
— Session 164027, Connector 3, Hyundai IONIQ 5 (DC2)
14:30:03
— Charging started (Transaction Id 164027).
14:52:28–14:52:34
— Vehicle sends a Pause command; charger switches to AVAILABLE → session ends.
📌
Note:
Between the PAUSE state and the appearance of the faults, there are no logs indicating cable disconnection and reconnection. We therefore assume the vehicle remained physically connected to the charger until the moment of failure.
From 14:52:39 onwards:
Abnormal cable temperature (DC2_CableTempSensor_XD101).
Insulation resistance dropped below threshold (IMD_BC2, 48kΩ).
DC contactor faults.
Error codes in DC2 module.
14:56:14–14:56:19:
Emergency Stop button pressed by customer.
Safety Relay (QA26) opened.
All PowerConverters report as FAULTED.
All connectors and outlets marked as out of order.
PLC and tripline failures.
Customer report from the field:
Customer noticed a strong burnt smell and smoke near the cable-vehicle connection point, pressed the Emergency Stop button, and was then unable to disconnect the cable from the vehicle.
Second Incident
— 04:26–04:50 PM, Connector 1, BMW (DC1)
Another critical event was detected:
04:26:56 PM:
Insulation resistance dropped to 142kΩ (IMD_BC1).
04:31:21 PM:
Critical drop to 111kΩ, all outlets set to out of order.
In the following minutes: loss of communication with all PowerConverters (CanCommLoss), E52/E7 error codes.
From 04:35:26 PM onwards:
FASTSHUTDOWN_CHECK
→ entire system locked in Faulted state.
Until
04:50 PM:
system did not recover automatically.
Customer report from the field:
Customer connected the cable to the vehicle, received an error message on the vehicle display, unplugged the cable, and was then unable to drive the vehicle — it had to be towed.
We would appreciate it if you could let us know:
1️⃣ When we can expect to receive your investigation report,
2️⃣ Whether there is any additional data we should provide to support the investigation.
Thank you very much for your cooperation and assistance!
Ziv Vinitzer
Head of DC Charging
